_meta.description: Forward-tuning overrides for PitchModelConfig, active for any sim date >= 2026-04-14 via should_use_forward_tuning(). Each key below has its own provenance block. See Syndicate/mlb_sim_accuracy_assessment_and_optimization_plan.md Phase 1 items #2/#3 for full context.

hr_rate_mult.description: Fitted via sweep_pm_hr_rate_mult.py against the 2026-season backfill (35 tune days / 11 disjoint holdout days, seed 2026, 100 sims/game), grid [0.95,1.00,1.10,1.20,1.30] vs 1.03 baseline, with hitter HR/props calibration explicitly disabled during the sweep so the raw parameter effect wasn't masked by the light-calibration band-aid already promoted in hitter_hr_calibration/default.json.
hr_rate_mult.rationale: Real, monotonic, correctly-directioned effect confirmed: raw hitter_hr_likelihood_topn_weighted.hr_avg_p rises with the multiplier (0.95->0.071, 1.03 baseline->0.077, 1.10->0.082, 1.30->0.097) while hr_brier improves alongside it (0.1086->0.1081->0.1066). 1.10 is the highest value that still clears the sweep's own holdout guardrail; 1.20 and 1.30 both improve hr_avg_p further but fail it. This closes roughly 13% of the diagnosed gap to the empirical HR rate (~0.125) -- a genuine, safe, small step, not a full fix.

xb_share_mult.description: Fitted via sweep_pm_xb_share_mult.py (pre-existing vendor tool, patched this session to disable hitter calibration during the sweep) against the same 35/11 backfill split, grid [0.80,0.85,0.90,1.00,1.10,1.20] vs 0.94 baseline. Targets the diagnosed excess-singles / under-projected-extra-base engine-shape defect directly -- xb_share_mult scales the singles-vs-extra-base split on contact.
xb_share_mult.rationale: The sweep tool's own best.json picks max(combined) among guardrail-passing candidates, which is backwards for this lower-is-better objective -- verified against the raw leaderboard instead. tune_combined improves monotonically from 0.80 to 1.20; only 1.00 and 1.20 fail the holdout guardrail, leaving 1.10 as the best safe candidate. Raw movement at 1.10 vs baseline: total_bases_4plus avg_p 0.117->0.123 (empirical target 0.152, ~17% of gap closed), total_bases_5plus 0.058->0.060 (target 0.070, ~20% closed). total_bases_1plus (the over-projection/excess-singles side) barely moves (0.6588->0.659) -- this is not a redistribution fix, it adds extra-base hits without correcting the singles excess, so that side of the defect remains fully open. hr_avg_p stays flat (0.0771->0.0772), confirming no interaction with the hr_rate_mult override above.

k_combine_log5_weight.description: Diagnosed via a 46-date/1209-start backtest against real market strikeout lines that batter-K-rate-vs-pitcher-K-rate combination used a plain 50/50 average, which structurally pulls every pitcher's per-PA strikeout target halfway toward the batter's (near-league-average) rate -- suppressing elite/ace projections and inflating back-end ones. Added k_combine_log5_weight as a shrinkage-weighted blend toward log5 (odds-ratio) combination, the same treatment hr/inplay_hit already get (see the _combined() comment in sim_engine/pitch_model.py). Validated at full backtest scale (same 46 tune+holdout dates, 100 sims/game, 1210 starts, 882 matched to real market K lines) via run_batch_eval_days.py, weight=1.0 (full log5) vs weight=0.0 (prior default).
k_combine_log5_weight.rationale: Real, correctly-directioned, statistically credible effect: corr(market_K_line, per-start prediction delta) = 0.283 (a smaller same-day sample without market-line control showed only 0.06 -- this is genuinely the signal, not noise). All four market-line tiers move the right way: elite bias -2.659->-2.585, mid-high -1.062->-1.046, mid +0.335->+0.274, back-end +1.048->+0.957. Full-game side effects at this scale are negligible-to-favorable (brier_home_win 0.2224->0.2245 flat, mae_total_runs 3.742->3.641 improved, mae_run_margin 3.323->3.370 flat) -- unlike the prior full k/bb/hbp log5 attempt that regressed full-game totals (see _combined()'s comment), applying log5 to K alone at real scale does not carry that cost. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this only closes ~3% of the diagnosed elite-tier gap (-2.659 -> -2.585 out of ~2.66 SO deficit). The bulk of the elite-pitcher strikeout gap is not from this per-PA-rate formula and is believed to come from workload/PA-count projection compression (stamina_pitches shrinkage toward a fixed prior) rather than K-rate combination -- see todo.md #178 for the open follow-up.

inplay_hit_combine_log5_weight.description: Diagnosed (todo.md part 9) that TEAM-level hits allowed -- all pitchers, not just starters -- are over-projected by +1.48/game (17.6% relative, n=1224 team-games). Tested reverting inplay_hit fully back to flat average (weight=0.0) via 46-date/100-sims backtesting, holding the other promoted fixes constant.
inplay_hit_combine_log5_weight.REVERTED_2026-08-01: Promoted to 0.0 first (see 'superseded_rationale' below), then reverted back to the original 1.0 (log5) the same session after building and finally running the betting-accuracy harness (grades the model's own P(over) against real market lines, not just mean-vs-actual bias -- built earlier in the session but not actually run until after this fix was already promoted). At weight=0.0 (flat average, what was briefly promoted), pooled real-money hit rate WORSENS on every market vs. the k_combine_log5_weight=1.0 + starter_quality_hook_weight=1.0 checkpoint that came right before it: strikeouts 55.78%->53.74%, hits_allowed 54.63%->53.08%, outs 59.54%->55.83% (n=882 each). That checkpoint (k+quality-hook, inplay still at log5) is strictly the best of all four tested states for betting accuracy -- it beats even the pre-session 'nothing promoted' baseline on strikeouts (52.49%) and outs (57.75%). The statistical-bias win (reducing mean hits-allowed error) is real, but it does not translate into better bets, and for a betting-intelligence platform the metric that actually matters is hit rate against the market's real lines, not mean-prediction bias in isolation. Lesson for next time: grade any pitch_model/manager_pitching change against betting_accuracy.py BEFORE promoting, not after -- bias/MAE improvements can trade away real edge (see market_blend_eval.py's docstring, which predicted this exact failure mode analytically before this fix was ever tested against it).
inplay_hit_combine_log5_weight.superseded_rationale: Broadly and consistently positive on STATISTICAL accuracy, not a narrow trade-off: TEAM-level hits bias improved from +1.482 to +0.821 (44.6% of the gap closed, n=1224), every market-line tier improved, and it unexpectedly also improved HR/total-bases calibration and full-game total-runs MAE. Real, small statistical costs: outs bias worsened modestly in 3 of 4 tiers, a mechanical interaction (fewer hits allowed -> more balls in play become outs -> pitcher reaches eff_hook sooner in outs terms). This looked like a clear net positive until graded against real betting outcomes.
